title: GET UP — THERE IS SIN IN THE CAMP

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Joshua, "Stand up! What are you doing down on your face? Israel has sinned; they have violated my covenant, which I commanded them to keep. They have taken some of the devoted things; they have stolen, they have lied, they have put them with their own possessions. That is why the Israelites cannot stand against their enemies; they turn their backs and run because they have been made liable to destruction. I will not be with you anymore unless you destroy whatever among you is devoted to destruction." — Josh 7:10-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's answer to Joshua is surprising. Joshua is lying on his face praying, and God says, "Stand up! What are you doing down on your face?" There is a time for prayer, and there is a time to get up and deal with the problem. Joshua was praying when he needed to be acting. Not all spiritual defeats are solved by more praying; some require us to address the sin we have been avoiding.

Then God names the real issue plainly: "Israel has sinned." Notice the honest list — they took, they stole, they lied, they hid. Sin is rarely a single act; it grows and multiplies. One act of greed led to theft, to deception, to concealment. Sin tolerated always spreads.

God's words are sobering: "I will not be with you anymore unless..." The loss at Ai was not bad luck or a stronger enemy; it was the withdrawal of God's presence because sin had been tolerated in the camp. This is a serious truth. Cherished, unconfessed sin genuinely hinders our fellowship with God and our effectiveness for Him.

But notice the mercy woven into the warning. God does not abandon Israel; He tells them exactly what is wrong and how to make it right. He wants to restore them. This is the heart of God even in confrontation — He exposes sin not to condemn but to cleanse. In Christ, God has dealt with our sin fully at the cross, and He still lovingly calls us to confess and forsake what hinders us, so that we may walk again in the joy of His presence.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there a problem in your life that calls for action, not just more prayer?
2. Have you let a "small" sin grow and spread by tolerating it?
3. How does it comfort you that God exposes sin in order to cleanse and restore?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, show me where I need to get up and deal with sin I have been avoiding. Thank You that You expose sin to cleanse me, not to condemn me. Amen.
